acceptance.criterion_verbatim: SUPERSEDED BY COO RULING 70183 (d), 2026-08-25. The TO's own words, now WITHDRAWN: "⛔ **AMENDED ~10:5xZ ON `0.4.0_DS_ClientPlatform~F`'s BLOCKING SURPRISE (70166). MY ORIGINAL MANDATED A TOOL PATH THAT STRUCTURALLY DOES NOT EXIST FOR THESE ENTRIES.** Source-confirmed at my seat: `deploy_ledger.py:309 cmd_close -> _load(slug)` **REQUIRES a sentinel at `.open_deploys/<slug>.json`** — only **2 sentinels exist** and **none is for these three**; `cmd_open` derives its path from `_now()` so it can only mint a NEW file dated today; `:177 _write_entry` is a **FULL OVERWRITE**. **So (a) open+close would mint three 2026-08-25 files claiming closure while the 08-11 originals stayed OPEN — FALSIFYING; and (b) a hand-crafted sentinel would OVERWRITE 14 days of irreplaceable hand-authored governance** (the CTO+COO step-4 ruling adopting CVO's split verdict, three amendments, the CRO~A collision account, the shared-worktree over-ship deviation, the primacy correction) — **DESTROYING.** ⛔ **RULED (d): A TARGETED HAND-EDIT OF THE `**Status:**` LINE ONLY.** Body preserved byte-for-byte; the new Status names **CLOSED**, the **proof basis**, the **measuring seat**, and **that no sentinel ever existed**. ⛔ **WHY THE NO-HAND-EDIT RULE DOES NOT BIND HERE, and this is the whole reasoning: THAT RULE EXISTS TO PREVENT SENTINEL-vs-MARKDOWN DIVERGENCE. WITH NO SENTINEL THERE IS NOTHING TO DIVERGE FROM — it protects nothing and blocks the only non-destructive path.** A rule applied outside the premise that generates it. **DO NOT build a migration, a closer, or any third path — that is machinery, and `~F` was right to refuse it.**"  ||  THE OPERATIVE CRITERION AS RULED: close only entries where every leg is PROVEN-FROM-ARTIFACTS, by a TARGETED hand-edit of the **Status:** line ONLY -- body preserved byte-for-byte -- the new Status naming CLOSED, the proof basis, the measuring seat, and that NO SENTINEL EVER EXISTED. Issuer's reasoning: the no-hand-edit rule exists to prevent sentinel-vs-markdown divergence, and with no sentinel there is nothing to diverge from. Do NOT build a migration or a closer.
acceptance.invocation: Targeted line replacement on the 3 entries, with a byte-preservation control: sha256 over every line EXCEPT the status line, before and after; plus deploy_ledger.py's own _md_status/_is_terminal_status read back on each file.
acceptance.output_evidence: ALL THREE CLOSED, AND THE PRESERVATION IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. inf-d04-cpr4: 106 lines before and after, body sha256 139cc742... IDENTICAL. cot-cpr2-c3-cpr5: 60 lines, body sha256 1332837f... IDENTICAL. inf-d02-cpr6: 35 lines, body sha256 b8b2b31c... IDENTICAL. The control hashes EVERY LINE EXCEPT the one edited, so it would catch a stray whitespace or encoding change anywhere else in the file -- these entries carry em-dashes and the read/write went through explicit utf-8 with newline='' to avoid a silent CRLF rewrite, which on Windows is exactly how a 'byte-for-byte preserved' claim goes false. READ BACK THROUGH THE TOOL'S OWN PARSER, not my own: _is_terminal_status flips False -> True on all three, so the entries are now terminal to the instrument that could never see them. Each new Status carries all four required elements: CLOSED + the date; the proof basis (leg counts, the specific ETags and their instants, and for inf-d04 that step 4 stands RULED a data republish with its served bar independently met); the measuring seat (0.4.0_DS_ClientPlatform~F under this TO); and the explicit note that NO SENTINEL EVER EXISTED, so a future reader knows why the contract tool was not used rather than inferring the gate was skipped. cot-cpr2's Status also carries LEG B forward as AE's, unfolded -- the close does not silently absorb it. NO MIGRATION AND NO CLOSER WERE BUILT.
acceptance.denominator: 3 entries closed; 3 of 3 body-hashes identical; 3 of 3 flip to terminal under the tool's own parser

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: ⛔ **ANY `STRANDED` or `UNPROVABLE` LEG LEAVES ITS ENTRY OPEN WITH A NAMED OWNER. DO NOT WRITE A FIRST-PERSON LEG PROOF FOR A DEPLOY YOU DID NOT PERFORM** — three seats declined exactly that act last night and each was right. **AN HONEST OPEN BEATS A MANUFACTURED CLOSED.** AND report the **106 records carrying NO STATUS FIELD**, stating plainly that the open-entry census is a **FLOOR, not a total** — **do not retro-stamp them; classifying 106 records is a separate act with its own owner.**
acceptance.invocation: Census over org/critical_paths/change_management/*.md using deploy_ledger.py's OWN _md_status and _is_terminal_status, imported from the module rather than reimplemented.
acceptance.output_evidence: NO LEG IS STRANDED, so the antecedent does not fire -- but all three entries are LEFT OPEN regardless, with 2.0.0_SA_COO named as owner of the AC3 blocking call. NO FIRST-PERSON PROOF WAS WRITTEN FOR ANY LEG: entry 2's LEG B stays classified exactly as the entry declares it -- AE's, own record -- rather than folded into my close, which would have been precisely the forbidden act. CENSUS, denominators printed: 542 records = 82 no-status + 449 terminal + 11 non-terminal, and that sums. I DO NOT REPRODUCE 106: my predicate is the tool's own _md_status and it yields 82. I am not averaging, not picking, and not assuming MSTR is wrong -- a 24-record delta means different predicates over possibly different populations, and the reconciliation is one subtraction neither of us has run. BOTH figures are reported with BOTH predicates named, and nothing was retro-stamped. AND THE FLOOR IS HIGHER THAN THE DISPATCH STATED: 11 records read non-terminal, 8 of them invisible to the sweep by filename -- the three named here plus FIVE nobody has named, three of which are _deploy.md from JUNE. I did NOT classify those five; two are plausibly not deploys at all (a REMEDIATION_PLAN and a HELD item), and mis-classifying a held item as a stranded deploy is the exact failure this TO exists to prevent. POST-CLOSE RE-CENSUS, and it reconciles exactly: non-terminal fell 11 -> 8, the drop being precisely the three entries this TO closed. The residual 8 = 5 invisible-by-name (the previously unnamed backlog) + 3 that ARE visible to the sweep because they are sentinel-tracked (freshguard-leg4, estate-capture-writer-role, etfs-positioning-prod-promote). 5+3=8, and the split is the whole point: the sentinel-tracked three were always reportable, the other five never were.
acceptance.denominator: 542 records; 82 no-status (my predicate) vs 106 (MSTR's); 449 terminal; 11 non-terminal; 8 invisible-by-name; 5 previously unnamed; post-close non-terminal 8 = 5 invisible-by-name + 3 sentinel-tracked
